messages:
taylor: quick note from paired onboarding this morning. new hire hit a surprising leak with the Go generator iterator in our example HTTP app. when the client closes the tab the handler returns but the iterator keeps producing tokens and a goroutine stays alive.

ben: can you paste the minimal handler you used?

taylor: yup: 
```go
func handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  iter := sdk.Generator("nano").Stream(r.Context(), Prompt{Text: "brief"})
  for iter.Next() {
    if _, err := w.Write([]byte(iter.Text())); err != nil {
      log.Println("write failed", err)
      return
    }
  }
  if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
    log.Println("iter err", err)
  }
}
```

ria: we have a long history of this pattern. root causes are usually: (1) auth refresh or reconnect using context.Background() so it ignores request cancel; (2) iterator internals block on transport read and have no explicit user-facing cancel.

ben: short-term fix: thread the request ctx into any background refresh (so refresh stops when req cancels) and change sampleapps to avoid Context.Background() in network code. long-term: add an explicit Close(ctx) on the iterator so handlers can deterministically tear down without cancelling the full req ctx.

ria: proposed API: 
```go
type GeneratorIter interface {
  Next() bool
  Text() string
  Err() error
  Close(ctx context.Context) error // idempotent, unblocks Next
}
```
Close(ctx) should attempt graceful shutdown, then force-close transport if ctx expires. Err() returns context.Canceled or ErrClosed after Close.

ben: +1. docs: add a small cookbook entry showing pattern: on write error call iter.Close(ctxWithTimeout) then return. also audit sampleapps for Context.Background() and update README to explain iterator semantics (Next blocks on network; Close is the proper shutdown).

sdk-bot: CI: go-sdk/streaming-tests passed on draft PR.

taylor: i'll open a PR with the API shim, two sampleapp changes (use Close on write errors), and a unit test that uses net.Pipe to emulate a server that keeps sending after Close. will include a short README snippet about avoiding Context.Background() in auth refresh.

ben: also add an integration test for auth-refresh mid-stream to ensure Close cancels reconnect. useful to prevent regressions.

ria: +1. small follow-up: consider a linter or grep check to flag Context.Background() in auth/transport code in repo to catch onboarding examples.

ben: agreed. thanks for the clear repro and plan. once PR is up I'll review.
